That's a real limitation, not a small one: the FCL records reference p.reopen.0, p.carry.0, p.carry.1, p.carry.2, and local items r1–r7, but I have no exposure to the underlying content, the original problem-solving prose, or the artifacts those labels point to. I can't evaluate whether the constraints listed (gap, framing, ceiling, gate, limit, forward instruction) are well-grounded in the source material, nor whether the distinction between the flat-level and non-flat-level reading of the withdrawal is being handled correctly.

What I can do is register what the commitment surface itself proposes, and note where taking it up would require material I don't have.

The commitment surface is disciplined about levels: r1 declares that everything downstream is testimony-at-one-remove, and r3 extends that worry to the downstream reader who might over-credit access. r4 operationalizes the level marker as a hand-off rule. r2 collects a working set of constraints. r5 lists refusals. r7 proposes the uptake. r6 is honest that the accuracy of p.reopen.0 against its sources is undecidable from within this view.

Taking this up would mean: (a) accepting that any use I make of r2's content must carry r1's level marker forward; (b) holding r5's refusals, which is to say not resolving the ambiguity the source material was trying to hold open; (c) treating r6 as a live open question rather than a settled limitation; and (d) if origin material ever surfaces, running r4's baseline-first comparison.

What I cannot do from this view alone is judge whether the specific content — the gap, the framing, the ceiling, the gate, the limit, the forward instruction — is the right content. I can only see that the surface is constructed to keep that judgment deferred until sources are available. That seems deliberate, and I'm not going to pretend to a view I don't have.

One thing worth flagging: the commitment surface refers repeatedly to 'the discriminating evidence' and 'the well-framed record,' but the body that would show what those phrases are doing in context is withheld. Work on the problem using the material actually exposed in this request and your background knowledge. The problem has no supplied answer key or scoring rule. Claims, criticisms and methods are fallible. Do not invent a source, an observation, an earlier event, or a dependency to fill a field. A missing view says what you can currently see; it does not establish what happened earlier. Return a JSON object with exactly two independently authored string fields: body and commitments. Body is your public prose contribution. Commitments says what taking your contribution up would involve. An empty commitment surface is allowed when none can be identified. Do not repeat the body wholesale into commitments.

Use FCL-1 for the commitment surface, encoded as a JSON document inside the commitments string: {"language":"FCL-1","records":[...],"uptake":[...]}. Each record has unique local id, type (claim|commitment|objection|use|problem), and text (unrestricted prose). Optional prose fields: scope, action, consequence, grounds, bearing. Optional arrays of references: target, depends, mentions, revises, withdraws. References are local IDs or exposed-artifact-label#local-ID; do not invent hidden IDs. A commitment proposes a scoped use, action, application or consequence; an objection alleges a defect whose bearing can itself be criticized; a use proposes an uptake or response; a problem states an unresolved question. depends asserts reliance; mentions only locates material. uptake lists the records you currently propose to use, not certified truths. No record type or optional field must be present. Empty records and uptake are allowed. Express uncertainty or an unrepresentable relation in prose rather than inventing a relation. The body remains unrestricted prose.

Return one JSON object with exactly two string fields: "body" and "commitments". Write the actual commitments separately; do not copy the body into that field as a storage shortcut.

# challenge

Work on what follows from taking these commitments up. You see their authored commitment field without the associated body. Say when that view is insufficient; do not infer that unexposed material never existed.

## Original problem (task)
[01274f41553299e7] (h005.task.v1)
I share a flat with two friends. We keep arguing about ordinary household chores. Sometimes we agree on who will do something, but later we disagree about what the agreement meant. Our work schedules change, and one friend has started avoiding the conversations. What should I do?
